title: 9.1 Small Group · Group 2
contentObjective: I can recognize when two quantities change together, and identify which one is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable, explain how I can tell, and judge a case I have not seen before.
languageObjective: I can justify my answer to a skeptic and connect it to a second strategy or representation.

conceptIntro.heading: Explore Relationships Between Two Variables
conceptIntro.intro: The same quantity can be independent in one situation and dependent in another. Always ask what is chosen.
conceptIntro.introEs: La misma cantidad puede ser independiente en una situación y dependiente en otra. Siempre pregunta qué se elige.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A variable is independent because it is chosen, not because it is time or because it comes first.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Una variable es independiente porque se elige, no porque sea el tiempo ni porque venga primero.

onMyOwn.problem: A movie theater is open 12 hours every day. On Monday it sells 150 tickets. On Tuesday it sells 210 tickets. Do the hours open depend on the tickets sold?
onMyOwn.problemEs: Un cine abre 12 horas todos los días. El lunes vende 150 boletos. El martes vende 210 boletos. ¿Las horas que abre dependen de los boletos vendidos?
choices: No. The hours stay 12 when the tickets change.
Yes. Selling more tickets means more hours.
Yes. The hours are the dependent variable.
choicesEs: No. Las horas siguen en 12 cuando cambian los boletos.
Sí. Vender más boletos quiere decir más horas.
Sí. Las horas son la variable dependiente.
choiceWhy: Tickets went from 150 to 210, but the hours stayed 12.
A dependent variable must change when the other changes. The hours did not change.
choiceWhyEs: Los boletos pasaron de 150 a 210, pero las horas siguieron en 12.
Una variable dependiente debe cambiar cuando cambia la otra. Las horas no cambiaron.

onMyOwn.explain: How can you tell that two quantities are not related?

onMyOwn.modelExplanation: Change one quantity and watch the other. Tickets went from 150 to 210, but the hours stayed 12. The hours do not change with tickets, so they do not depend on them.
onMyOwn.modelExplanationEs: Cambia una cantidad y observa la otra. Los boletos pasaron de 150 a 210, pero las horas siguieron en 12. Las horas no cambian con los boletos, así que no dependen de ellos.

check.stem: The number of pizzas made each week determines other costs at the shop. Which variable is the independent variable in this relationship?
check.explanation: The number of pizzas is independent because it is the value that determines the other costs. Cost of cheese is dependent because it changes as a result of pizzas made; the number of employees and toppings allowed are fixed limits, not quantities that change with pizza count.

check.explanationEs: El número de pizzas es independiente porque es el valor que determina los demás costos. El costo del queso es dependiente porque cambia como resultado de las pizzas que se hacen; el número de empleados y los ingredientes permitidos son límites fijos, no cantidades que cambian con el número de pizzas.

cost of cheese and number of pizzas made

extending.modelAnswer: Devon used the rule “whatever happens first in time is the independent variable.” That rule fails because the roles depend on what is chosen, not on what happens first. The shop chooses the number of pizzas, so pizzas is the independent variable, and the cheese used responds to that choice — cheese is dependent.
extending.modelAnswerEs: Devon usó la regla “lo que ocurre primero en el tiempo es la variable independiente”. extending.stem: Claim: “The dependent variable always has the larger values.” Is this claim always, sometimes, or never true?

extending.explanation: Sometimes. Jog for 90 minutes and you might run 9 miles — the dependent value (9) is smaller. revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Selling Pizzas
revealWordProblem.text:
At a local pizza shop, a customer can order a large pizza with up to three different toppings for $12.49. The shop is open daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and has a total of 6 employees. The shop spends $1.15 on cheese and $1.95 on sauce for each pizza.
Question: How would you describe the relationship between the number of large pizzas sold and each of the following: the hours the shop is open, the number of employees who work in the shop, the cost of cheese each week, and the cost of sauce each week?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A pizzeria sign showing hours of 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and a large pizza with up to 3 toppings for $12.49.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Sort each pair by whether one quantity depends on the other. The hours the shop is open do not change when more pizzas sell — the shop is open 11 to 9 either way — so the hours are independent of pizza sales. The number of employees is also independent day to day; 6 people work whether the shop sells 40 pizzas or 90. Cheese cost does depend on pizzas sold: every pizza uses $1.15 of cheese, so weekly cheese cost = 1.15p, where p is the number of pizzas. Sauce works the same way at $1.95 a pizza, so weekly sauce cost = 1.95p. In both of those, p is the independent variable and the cost is the dependent variable, and each cost grows at a steady rate as p grows.
